title: Reveal the unsure route after a delay
statement: Reveal an 'I'm not sure' route to help after a learner has been stuck a while, because shown up front the choice that can't be wrong becomes the cheap path.
example: One reading build reveals the route after about 20 seconds, below the options.
detail: Every lesson in a Grade 3 reading build authored a branch for the child who freezes, with its own gentler turns, but none of it could run: the player classified only taps, so a child with no answer had to guess and got the wrong conversation. A quiet 'I'm not sure yet' door now routes there, revealed after about 20 seconds below the options. The build's rules give the reason for the delay: it is the one button on screen that cannot be wrong, so mounted with the options it becomes the cheap path and children who would have answered take it. Because the door is mounted on every check, a lesson missing the branch gives it a dead end, which the rules count as a defect.

evidence.quote: An authored branch nothing can reach is not a feature, it is a file.
An escape hatch offered up front stops being an escape hatch.
It is the one button on screen that cannot be wrong, so mounted with the options it becomes the *cheap path* and children who would have answered take it.
A lesson missing the branch therefore has a door onto a **dead end**, found by the freezing child.
